title: Vela app manifest v3 (managed web app)
description: A managed web app is an existing self-hosted web server that Vela installs, starts as a local native service and publishes on its own web address. The application keeps its own interface, accounts and data format; Vela owns the installation record, the service lifetime, the gateway and the declared recovery operations. A v3 manifest never grants the browser SDK bridge, app storage, actions, widgets or agent access.

version.description: The packaged release of this app, as the package author versions it.

compatibility.description: What the package needs from the host. `managedService` is the host feature revision; a host that does not implement it must refuse the package rather than ignore the declaration.

managedService.description: The managed-service feature revision this package needs. A host that implements a different one refuses the package with an actionable message rather than ignoring declarations it cannot honour, so this is a number to compare rather than a constant.

source.description: Where the upstream application comes from, so an install review can say whose code is about to run with the user's own permissions.

trust.description: Trusted native execution: the service runs as the Vela host user with that user's operating-system permissions. It is not a sandbox, and no other value is accepted.

artifacts.description: One entry per supported operating system and CPU architecture. There is no combined `posix` target: a host picks the entry that matches both its OS and its architecture, and refuses to run anything when none matches.

args.description: The argument vector passed to the executable. No shell is involved. Each item may contain the bounded placeholders {port}, {host}, {dataDir}, {codeDir}, {publicUrl} and {appId}.

workingDirectory.description: Which of the app's own directories the process starts in.

environment.description: Reviewed, non-secret environment values added to a minimal inherited environment. Placeholders are the same bounded set the arguments use. Vela credentials are never placed here.

bind.description: The loopback address the service is expected to listen on. The port is allocated by the host and supplied through {port}.

basePath.description: Where the application serves its own root. Managed apps are published at the root of their own web address, so this is "/" unless the upstream server insists otherwise.

websocket.description: Whether the application needs WebSocket upgrades through the gateway. "unsupported" makes the gateway refuse upgrades with a stated reason rather than hanging.

readiness.description: The HTTP probe that decides the service is really serving. A listening socket is not readiness.

startWithVela.description: The package's suggested default. The user's own choice is stored by the host and always wins.

stopTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a graceful stop is given before the owned process tree is forced.

data.description: The one directory the application keeps its data in. It survives Stop, a Vela restart, a code replacement and removal of the app.

directory.description: Relative to the app's own managed data root. Never an arbitrary host folder.

backup.description: How a consistent snapshot is taken. "stop-and-copy" stops the service first, which is the only method this host revision implements.

embedding.description: Whether the application may be shown inside a Vela window. "auto" tries the window and keeps the full-page route; "external" always opens a separate tab because upstream frame rules forbid embedding. Vela never strips an upstream frame defence to force a window.

integration.description: Deliberately absent by default. Installing a managed app grants no SDK bridge, app storage, actions, widgets, assistant or agent access, and these flags exist so a package cannot imply otherwise.

file.description: An archive carried inside the package itself. Use this or `url`, never both.

url.description: An HTTPS archive fetched during install review. The download is completed and verified against `sha256` before anything is approved, and approval is bound to those bytes.

size.description: Exact archive size in bytes. A download that does not match is refused before extraction.

executable.description: The program to run, relative to the extracted archive root.

expandedSizeLimit.description: Upper bound on the extracted tree, in bytes. The host applies its own ceiling as well.
